problem: Frontier-based and end-to-end ObjectNav methods only react to the observed map, and prior map-completion ('imagination') works are limited in scalability, use unrealistic random masking, or are evaluated as vision tasks instead of by navigation performance.
motivation: Humans infer the layout and likely object locations of unseen regions from partial views and prior knowledge. Predicting unobserved geometry and semantics should give the agent better long-term goals and shorter paths. The paper therefore trains a network to complete a partial map and evaluates it in closed-loop navigation.
key_idea: Train a network to predict the complete geometry (occupancy) and CLIP semantic features of a scene from a partial BEV GeoSem Map, then pick long-term navigation goals from the similarity between the imagined map and the goal query.
insight: Occupancy imagination shortens paths: in PointNav the UNet+BCE imagination agent reaches goals in 439 mean steps versus 640 for the vanilla replanning agent, about a 1.5x speedup. UNet beats the MAE-ViT (completion 1.0 vs 0.85-0.89), and BCE is slightly better than MSE. For ObjectNav, imagined CLIP features give small gains over VLFM-CLIP (SPL 0.67 vs 0.66, success 0.73 vs 0.71). Training on masks generated by simulating agent navigation is meant to match test-time partial observations, but no ablation isolates this choice.
method: GeoSem Map: 224x224x(512+1) BEV grid storing per-cell CLIP features (LSeg pixel embeddings back-projected with depth and pose, averaged per cell) and occupancy in {0 free, 0.5 unknown, 1 occupied}. Occupancy is height-filtered (30%-70% of scene height, drone-like) with a 10%-of-max density threshold.
Imagination Module: a UNet (channels 64-1024) or MAE-ViT-base maps the partial GeoSem Map to a full map with CLIP features, occupancy probability and an interior-mask probability.

Training data via simulated agents: for each of 3000 Structured3D training scenes, an A* agent with limited FOV and sensor range travels between random waypoints in a 2D grid world. The partially observed maps it accumulates serve as inputs, with rotation and scaling augmentation.
Multi-task loss: 10*(cosine CLIP loss on interior cells) + 1*(weighted BCE occupancy) + 1*(BCE interior mask). The interior mask restricts goal search because exterior cells get no CLIP supervision.

Long-term goal extraction: cosine similarity between the imagined CLIP map (interior only) and the text CLIP embedding of the goal is normalized and thresholded. DBSCAN removes outliers, silhouette score picks K, and a K-component GMM gives candidate zones. The cluster closest to the agent is chosen, and A* plans on the imagined occupancy.

Update rule: re-imagine and reselect the goal when the current FOV overlaps little with the FOV at the last update. Exploration ends once the goal cell is observed, and the agent then navigates directly to it.

GT GeoSem construction: Structured3D equirectangular RGBD is converted into 12 perspective views (90° FOV) for LSeg, with an index map preserving pixel-to-3D-point correspondence. An interior/exterior mask suppresses wall leaks.

setting.backbone: UNet imagination network (trained from scratch) + frozen LSeg / CLIP ViT-B/32; A* planner; ViT (MAE) as ablation
setting.training_data: Structured3D, 3000 training scenes, with partial occupancy masks generated by simulated agents; the 500 validation scenes are used for evaluation.
setting.observation: Simulated egocentric RGB-D + pose in a 2D grid world, with a LIDAR-like depth sensor with limited FOV and range; the evaluation uses a precomputed GT GeoSem Map
setting.action_space: Discrete: MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK UP/DOWN 30°, STOP; long-term goals are chosen on the map and executed by A*
setting.simulator: Custom 2D grid world built on Structured3D
setting.privileged: Goal detection is assumed when the goal cell is observed in the occupancy map (P[gx,gy] != 0.5), and observations are simulated from GT maps; no other GT information at test time

numbers.extra: Custom 2D grid-world benchmark, 6 categories; goal assumed detected when observed; imagination trained on Structured3D train scenes
Two sequential waypoints, max 3000 timesteps, replanning every 10 steps; occupancy only

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks on Structured3D only; no standard benchmark such as HM3D/MP3D ObjectNav is reported. Metrics printed as fractions were converted to percent for SPL and SR.
results: On the Structured3D-validation ObjectNav benchmark, ForesightNav reaches SPL 0.67, success 0.73 and distance-to-goal 25.32, versus VLFM-CLIP at 0.66 / 0.71 / 27.36, StructNav-Frontiers at 0.63 / 0.66 and Random at 0.62 / 0.68. On PointNav, imagination gives 100% completion and about 1.5x fewer steps than the vanilla agent (439 vs 641).
limitations: Evaluation is only in a 2D grid world on synthetic Structured3D, with simulated detection and no real robot or 3D simulator. The margins over VLFM-CLIP are small and no variance is reported.
The 224x224 BEV map limits scaling to large scenes and non-object-centric queries; higher resolution would greatly increase memory and network size.
Baselines are re-implemented variants (VLFM with CLIP, StructNav with a top-down semantic map), so comparisons are not against the original systems.
